newsitem.title: CHILE: Electricals push Chilean stocks higher to close.
newsitem.headline: Electricals push Chilean stocks higher to close.

text.p: Soaring electrical stocks pushed Chilean shares higher in afternoon trading and moved blue chips up over a full point by the close.

Rumors of a merger by the Chispa Uno and Chispa Dos investment societies and continued speculation that Endesa of Spain might buy part of Chile's own Endesa continued to drive the market, brokers said.
The blue-chip IPSA closed 1.16 percent higher to 97.72 points. The all-share IGPA ended 0.36 percent higher to 5345.51 points on moderate volume of 14.4 billion pesos.
"The market is looking stronger. But there are a lot of rumors going around and people aren't sure which to believe," said one broker.

Attention focused on the electrical sector, where investment societies related to Enersis posted some of the sharpest gains. Enersis holds the largest single stake at 25 percent in the Chilean Endesa.

Reports circulated that the two Chispa groups might merge and that Endesa of Spain would enter the Chilean market through the Chispas or through another Enersis investment society -- driving all of them sharply higher.
Chispa Uno A series rose 4.51 percent to 179.75 pesos, while Chispa Dos A series ended 4.65 percent higher to 180 pesos. Almendros A series also climbed 4.65 percent to 180 pesos.

Stocks in the Soquimich group also posted major gains on rumors of new industrial investments in the group, brokers said. Oro Blanco was up 15 percent to 3.29 pesos, and Nortegrande close 10 percent higher to 7.8 pesos.
Iansa's parent company Campos rose 6.7 percent to 103.5 pesos, partly on Iansa's announcement that it was moving into the Brazil food processing business, a broker said.
Brokers said the market looked strong going into next week and that it appeared to be regaining its footing after weeks of generally soft prices and sluggish volume.

Decliners included Santa Rita, down 2.1 percent to 46 pesos, and Enersis, which dipped 0.2 percent to 252 pesos as most buying in the electrical sector went to the investment societies rather than to Enersis itself.
